I can write all of this by hand, and for most of my career I did. I work through AI agents now because they produce code far faster than I can. I decide what gets built and how, I tell them, and I review what comes back. Nothing is finished until I have confirmed it is correct. What took me a month now takes a day or a week, and I would put the change at 10 to 100 times. That is my own statement from doing the work rather than a measurement, so read it beside the dates here.

documents.t: I am Ahsan Mahmood, a full-stack developer in Lahore. This guide sits beside my portfolio: the projects I can show, the work I take on, and the released products I have built with Zaions. I have more than eight years of hands-on development experience. I can write the code myself. Today I also direct AI agents, read what they produce and check the result against the product people will actually use. The difference matters at both ends of a build. Choosing what to make, setting boundaries and deciding whether the finished work is correct still take experience. An agent can move quickly through an implementation; it cannot take responsibility for the decision to ship it. That remains mine.

I want the working product to carry more weight than a claim about it. A client project I can show belongs here. So do my skills and the products that are live. Each release in the ecosystem has a direct destination; you can leave this guide and inspect it yourself. A private or unfinished project does not join that list because a polished description would tell you less than a working page. The comparison pages in this guide describe ways of getting software built. They do not compare other people's profiles. They explain the decisions a buyer will face when choosing an agency, a marketplace, an early-career developer or one person who can carry the work from scope to release. The answer depends on the job. The dates, prices and limits on the main site are there so you can decide with more than a slogan.

These dates describe this site, not a delivery promise for somebody else's project. 31 July 2026: Planning and the first design pages began. 16 August 2026: The rebuilt app received its first commit. 21 August 2026: The rebuild took over aoneahsan.com. 5 November 2026: The site moved to a new host. The design pages came before the rebuilt app. The live site then gave the work a harder test: pages had to render, links had to arrive at the right place, and the build had to keep serving after I stopped looking at it. The guide you are reading is part of the same record. It explains the work without requiring someone to sign in first.

I decide what gets built. Then I check it. Agents help me move through implementation, but the code, browser behaviour and handover still need review. A green build is one piece of evidence; it does not tell me whether a person can finish the task on a phone, whether a link leads to a live release, or whether an answer on a public page is true. If you have a project in mind, contact me through the portfolio. Tell me what it needs to do. I will look at the work and say where I fit. You can also browse the released Zaions products or visit Zaions to see the team around them.

An agency sells you a team under one contract. I am one developer who directs AI agents. For some jobs the team is plainly the better buy. Choose it when the work needs several people at the same hour.
documents.s: Hiring an agency or hiring me — Ahsan Mahmood

documents.t: An agency is the better choice when the work needs several people at the same hour: a large build on a fixed date, brand and illustration alongside the code, or round-the-clock support with a rota behind it. I am one person, and I am not a designer. It is also right when you want one contract to cover design, development and support for years, with the agency deciding who does each part.

A team under one contract: usually an account manager, a designer, a few developers and someone checking the work. You talk to the account manager, and the account manager talks to the people building it. A good agency has a process and a bench. If a developer leaves or falls ill, somebody else picks the work up and you may never hear about it.

Clutch's 2026 guide says software development projects reviewed on its directory typically cost $10,000–$49,999. That describes projects reported to Clutch, not a quote from every agency. Ask two or three agencies for a written quote against the same brief you would send me. Compare the scope and support in each quote as carefully as the total. Sources checked 27 November 2026: Clutch, Software Development Company Pricing Guide 2026 (checked 27 November 2026).

You talk to the person doing the work. The person who models the data also writes the security rules, packages the Android build and answers the store reviewer, so nothing gets lost between a brief and a developer. The team I direct is AI agents rather than staff. They write the code far faster than I can, and I decide what they build, review what comes back and run it before you hear about it. There is no handover between people for a detail to fall through. The handover assumes I am not available: full IP transfer, and documentation that matches the code.

documents.t: A marketplace gives you a long list of people and a way to hold the money until you approve. The difficulty is telling, before you have paid, which kind of person you have found. Choose it for a small job with a clear finish.
documents.s: A marketplace freelancer or me — Ahsan Mahmood

documents.t: For a small job with a clear finish, a marketplace is hard to beat: a bug fix, a landing page, one screen built from a design you already have. Its escrow and dispute process are also real protection, and a direct arrangement with me does not come with them. If that matters most to you, stay on the platform.

A search box, a long list of profiles, and bids that arrive quickly. You choose from ratings, a portfolio and a short message, and the platform holds the money until you approve the work. The person you get might be excellent. A rating tells you that earlier buyers were happy with earlier jobs, and those jobs may look nothing like yours.

Freelancer.com lists an employer fee of 3% or $3, whichever is greater, when a fixed-price project is awarded. Its hourly-project fee is 3% of each payment. The freelancer sets the project rate separately. That is one marketplace's published fee, not a universal rate. Read the fee page for the service you use before accepting a bid. Sources checked 27 November 2026: Freelancer.com, fees and charges for employers (checked 27 November 2026).

You do not have to trust a rating. Everything I have built that can be shown is on this site with a link that opens it: you can use the live products before you write to me. Scoping happens on a call, before any number. A fixed number attached to an unscoped brief is a number one of us is going to be unhappy about, and the call is where I say whether I am the right person. The cost of that is time up front. A call and a written scope are slower than accepting a bid, and for a small job they are not worth it.

documents.t: Your own team knows your business and stays. If the software is the business, that is where it belongs in the end. The question is what happens before that team exists. Choose it when the software is the business and needs someone every day for years.
documents.s: Building in-house or hiring me — Ahsan Mahmood

documents.t: If the software is the business and it will need someone every day for years, build the team. No outside developer should be the long-term answer for your core product. In-house is also right when the knowledge cannot leave the building, or when you already have engineers and a settled roadmap.

Your own employee or team: someone who knows the business, sits in your meetings and still remembers why a decision was made three years later. It is usually the slowest route to start, because you have to find them, hire them and keep them busy once the first release is out.

In May 2025 the median wage of a US software developer was $135,980 a year. The lowest-paid tenth earned less than $82,460 and the highest-paid tenth more than $214,670. That is the wage alone. Recruiting, benefits and equipment come on top of it. Source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Software Developers (May 2025 wages, checked 27 November 2026)

I fit the stretch before that: the first release, the codebase that needs rescuing, the product your team has no time to start. Taking over someone else's code usually begins with an audit and a prioritised roadmap. You get a product without a hiring round, and the handover assumes I am not available. You are not buying a codebase only I can read. If the project only runs while I am on it, I have not finished. And if the right answer turns out to be hiring a senior who works this way, I am open to remote roles too.

documents.t: A newer developer costs less and often works hard. What you are short of is someone who has already seen how this kind of project goes wrong. Choose it when the job is small and the mistakes are cheap.
documents.s: An inexperienced developer or me — Ahsan Mahmood

documents.t: This is the better choice when the job is small and the mistakes are cheap: a brochure site, an internal script, a prototype you will throw away. It is also right when you already have a senior who can review the work and you want to train someone. Paying me for that buys more than you need.

A lower rate and, often, real energy. Someone early in their career will usually take work a senior would turn down, and plenty of them learn quickly. You also become the senior. Someone has to decide the architecture, read the code and spot what will break in a year. If nobody does, it does not get done.

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics does not split developer pay by experience. Its nearest figure is the bottom of the range: in May 2025 the lowest-paid tenth of US software developers earned less than $82,460 a year. That is a US employee's wage, not a freelance rate, and pay in other countries is very different. Source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Software Developers (May 2025 wages, checked 27 November 2026)

I have been shipping production software since January 2018, at five companies and then on my own. Much of that experience is a list of things I have already got wrong. The exam platform went down because a free-tier read quota ran out, and every list query I have written since has carried an explicit limit. Experience also decides what happens with AI agents. An agent writes whatever it is told, with the same confidence whether the idea is good or bad. Knowing which is which is the part of the job I kept for myself. And I can still write it by hand. When an agent goes the wrong way, I can see where, and I can take over rather than asking it to guess again.

documents.t: A vibe coder describes an app to an AI tool and ships what comes out, without an engineering background behind it. I use the same kind of tools, so speed is not what separates us. Choose it when you want to test an idea on real people this week.
documents.s: A vibe coder or me — Ahsan Mahmood

documents.t: For a demo, a landing page or an idea you want to try on real people this week, this is the right call. Nobody should pay a senior developer to find out whether anyone wants the thing. If it works, you will know what to build properly, and you will have spent very little to learn it.

Someone with no engineering background, or you yourself, describing an app to an AI tool and shipping what comes out. The first version can appear in an afternoon, and it can look finished. What you do not get is anyone who can tell you whether it is finished. The tool will say that it is.

Bolt lists a Pro plan at $25 a month with monthly billing. Lovable's docs list Pro from $25 a month for 100 credits. Replit lists its plans separately; check each provider's current allowance as well as its price. Those are tool subscriptions. Someone still has to check the work, maintain it and pay for what the finished app uses. Sources checked 27 November 2026: Bolt, pricing (monthly billing, checked 27 November 2026), Lovable, subscription plans (checked 27 November 2026), Replit, pricing (checked 27 November 2026).

The difference is what happens after the agent says it is done. I read the code, run the real flow as a real user, check the security rules and look at what the database allows. A demo and a product look the same until someone signs in with the wrong account, a quota runs out or the store reviewer writes back. A green build is not evidence that a feature works. The first two days of rebuilding this site, below, are the example I would point at: eight defects that the automated checks had passed. That review is the slow part, and it stays with me. Agents made the writing fast; they did not make the checking fast.

documents.t: AChat makes the first contact a choice. I can point to its web and Android app, and to the three ways someone can find another person without exchanging a phone number. The question: How can people connect without sharing a phone number?

A username, invitation link or QR code gives a person a way to reach someone they chose. That is a narrower request than handing over a phone number. The product also has anonymous rooms that can be opened without an account.
documents.s: What changes at the first invitation?

documents.t: The released web app is the direct destination here. The roster also records an Android surface. I would check those actual entry points before describing a messaging experience as shipped.

The published facts describe discovery and anonymous rooms. They do not promise that every conversation is anonymous or that no information is ever stored. A useful portfolio page should keep that distinction visible.

A username, an invite link and a QR code all solve the first contact, but they ask different things of the people using them. The published release gives those choices alongside an anonymous room that does not need an account. I would inspect each entry point on the live web app, then check the Android surface recorded for the same product. The useful engineering question is whether a person can tell which kind of conversation they are entering before they share an address or start a room. The roster gives the routes into a chat. It does not settle every privacy question about the chat afterward.
documents.s: Why keep these ways of meeting separate?

documents.t: AChat is a messaging app on the web and Android for chosen people. People can find a user by username, invite link or QR code without a phone number. Anonymous rooms can be opened without an account.
Visit AchatAI Read AchatAI documentation See all released Zaions products

CallVault keeps the phone library at the centre of the experience. A person can play, search, annotate and export recordings there; private cloud backup is something they choose to enable. The question: When does a call recording leave the phone?

The app records calls through the audio source a phone makes available. That qualification matters: Android devices and call routes differ, so the page should not promise a uniform capture result on every handset.
Playback, search and notes make a recording useful after the call. Export is an explicit action from the phone library rather than a reason to move every file to a server by default.
documents.s: How is a recording found later?

documents.t: The roster says recordings stay on the phone unless private cloud backup is enabled. I would check that choice in the app before describing its data flow more broadly.
documents.s: What stays under the user’s control?

documents.t: Backup does. The phone library already has playback, search, notes and export, so the recording can be useful without first moving it to a cloud account. Private cloud backup is a choice the person enables. That order is significant for an app handling call audio: a list of features is less useful than knowing where the file stays until somebody asks otherwise. I would inspect the backup control and an exported recording on the released Android app, then check the actual audio source on the device being used. The published product cannot make every handset supply the same source.

I would inspect a run of check-ins with a gap, then check whether the visual still tells the truth without a contest attached. The web and Android surfaces are both recorded for one account. I would inspect both the immediate rule and its scheduled version, including how the app shows which connection type is affected. The roster establishes the available controls.
